anomalies.observed: The VDD/VCC supply pins of both SC16IS752 UARTs (U16, U25), both MCP2515 CAN controllers (U39, U45) and both isolator VCC1 pins (U8, U48) sit on net NET0028. That net has no power label and no connection to +3V3 or any other supply. Its only other connections are decoupling capacitors to GND and reset/interrupt pull-ups to the same node.
anomalies.expected: These logic supply pins should be on the 3.3V logic rail (+3V3), which the reset and interrupt pull-ups and decoupling caps appear designed around. The board's 3.3V logic devices should be powered.
anomalies.impact: If NET0028 is truly unpowered, the CAN controllers, UARTs and CAN isolator logic side would have no supply, so CAN and serial communication would fail. The reset and interrupt pull-ups would also float to nothing.

anomalies.observed: R38 is valued "24k" but its selected part is described as a 24Ω resistor, with MPN FRC0805J240TSD (the '240' code denotes 24Ω).
anomalies.expected: The value field should match the chosen part. If 24k is intended, the part should be a 24kΩ resistor; if 24Ω is the part, the value should read 24Ω.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R38") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: The part actually placed may be a 24Ω resistor across the VOUTP/VOUTN rails. That would draw large current and dissipate heavily, or else the value and part disagree and the BOM is wrong.

anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers have GND2 (pin 5) and GND1 (pin 4) tied to the same board GND net, so the isolated side shares ground with the main board.
anomalies.expected: An isolated CAN transceiver should have GND2 on an isolated ground, separate from GND1, to provide the galvanic isolation the design calls for.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier is defeated, so the CAN buses are not galvanically isolated from the board ground, leaving them exposed to ground loops and faults the isolator was meant to block.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows the 3.3V logic devices (UARTs, CAN controllers, isolator logic sides) on a floating unlabeled net NET0028 with no supply connection, which is the most likely fault. Lower-confidence concerns are the 24k/24Ω value mismatch on R38 and the isolated CAN GND2 pins tied to board GND.
